title: ALL THE PEOPLE, TOGETHER BEFORE GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: All the Israelites, with their elders, officials and judges, were standing on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the Lord, facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Both the foreigners living among them and the native-born were there. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord had formerly commanded when he gave instructions to bless the people of Israel. — Josh 8:33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture this scene. The whole nation gathered between two mountains — elders, officials, judges, and ordinary people, all standing together before the ark of God. This was not a gathering for the leaders alone, nor for the spiritually elite. Every person was there, giving their attention to God and His covenant. God's word and worship were for all His people together.

Look closely at one beautiful detail: "Both the foreigners living among them and the native-born were there." The outsiders, the non-Israelites who had joined themselves to God's people, stood right alongside the native-born. There was a place among God's people for those who came from outside. This reflects the heart of God, whose purposes were never meant for one nation alone. Even here, in the Old Testament, the door was open to the outsider who would come and worship the true God.

This foreshadows a glorious New Testament reality. In Christ, the dividing wall between "insider" and "outsider" has been broken down. Paul writes that in Christ "there is neither Jew nor Gentile... for you are all one" (Gal 3:28). People from every nation and background are brought together into one family, standing as equals before God. The foreigners at Mount Ebal were an early glimpse of the countless multitude from every tribe and tongue who will one day worship together (Rev 7:9).

What unites God's people is not race or status but our shared standing before Him. Whatever our background, we come to the same God, through the same Saviour, and stand together as one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you value gathering with all of God's people, not just a select few?
2. How does it move you that even here, the "foreigner" had a place among God's people?
3. Are you helping break down barriers so that "outsiders" find their place in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ You gather people from every background into one family. Help me welcome others and treasure our shared standing before You. Amen.
